<p style="text-align: center;"><span style="font-family: Arvo; font-size: 13px; color: #8a8a95;">Updated September 2026</span></p>
[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="10"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]<span style="font-family: Arvo;"><strong>Oddtoe</strong> is an experiential design and generative-AI animation studio based in Melbourne, creating projection, installation, and animated work for events, venues, and galleries. This is a <strong>use case</strong>: how a campaign uses <strong>Oddtoe</strong> to pull off a <strong>publicity stunt</strong> or a cheeky PR campaign, from the first idea to the photograph that gets printed. The worked example is a set of carried heads. The same steps apply to an inflatable politician, projected animation for a protest, an ironic mascot costume, or a kinetic sculpture.</span>[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]<span style="font-family: Arvo;">Come to <strong>Oddtoe</strong> for visual art with a point, designed by a <strong>political cartoonist</strong> — chief designer for a Washington DC paper, and an editorial cartoonist before that. That background matters here, because a photograph at a rally and a daily cartoon are the same problem. You get one picture to make the argument, and nobody sticks around for an explanation. The stunts people remember passed that test: the <strong>Trump baby blimp</strong> over Parliament Square, or the <strong>pink boat Extinction Rebellion</strong> parked in Oxford Circus.</span>[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" What could that <strong>front-page photo</strong> look like? How can <strong>your brand or movement go viral</strong>? Art and humour are <strong>Oddtoe's thing</strong>. The idea, the feeling the art stirs, and your organisation's message all get worked out here.
</span>[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][vc_single_image image="16318" img_size="640x480" style="vc_box_rounded" css=""][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="22" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="22" screen_tablet_spacer_size="16" screen_mobile_spacer_size="16"][dfd_heading content_alignment="text-left" enable_delimiter="" subtitle_google_fonts="yes" subtitle_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3A700|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal" style="style_02" subtitle="STEP TWO" title_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:30|font_family:BebasNeueRegular|line_height:30|letter_spacing:0" subtitle_font_options="tag:div|font_size:12|line_height:16|color:%238a9f6a|letter_spacing:1" heading_margin="margin-bottom:12px;" subheading_margin="margin-bottom:6px;"]Sketching[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text css=""]<span style="font-family: Arvo;">Everything starts <strong>on paper, on a grid</strong>. Proportions get argued out flat, front and side, long before anything gets cut. Here, a series of politicians' heads are sketched with the poles that the protesters will carry. Get the sketch right and the <strong>impact of the art</strong> shows for the first time. </span>[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][vc_single_image image="16274" img_size="640x480" style="vc_box_rounded" css=""][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="22" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="22" screen_tablet_spacer_size="16" screen_mobile_spacer_size="16"][dfd_heading content_alignment="text-left" enable_delimiter="" subtitle_google_fonts="yes" subtitle_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3A700|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal" style="style_02" subtitle="STEP THREE" title_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:30|font_family:BebasNeueRegular|line_height:30|letter_spacing:0" subtitle_font_options="tag:div|font_size:12|color:%238a9f6a|line_height:16|letter_spacing:1" heading_margin="margin-bottom:12px;" subheading_margin="margin-bottom:6px;"]Humans &amp; Movement[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text css=""]<span style="font-family: Arvo;">Working out how anyone <em>actually</em> carries the art. Where they stand, how many people it takes, how the weight sits on a shoulder <strong>after an hour</strong>, whether it can turn a corner without a traffic jam forming. <strong>Oddtoe</strong> works out the carrying and the moving for you. Leave it until the morning of the march and you are solving it in a crowd.</span>[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" scale</strong>, parked where a rally is already going on. Nobody had to stage anything. Out come the phones.</span>

<span style="font-family: Arvo;">So what does a stunt like this do for your numbers? Quite a lot, and all of it can be counted: coverage, shares, search traffic in the <strong>two days after</strong>, and the figures your board actually reads.</span>[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="18" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="18" screen_tablet_spacer_size="18" screen_mobile_spacer_size="18"][dfd_icon_list icon_margin="16" icon_bottom_spase="14" main_style="style-1" icon_size="30" icon_dec_size="50" icon_border_style="solid" icon_color="#ddccb1" font_options="line_height:20"][dfd_icon_list_item icon="dfd-icon-newspaper"]

screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]<span style="font-family: Arvo;">Non-profits and NGOs, grassroots campaigns, unions, advocacy organisations, political campaigns, and PR agencies with a brand that wants a publicity stunt. What they all have is <strong>a date in the diary</strong> and something they need people to see.</span>

<span style="font-family: Arvo;"><strong>Campaigns with a fixed date</strong> — a launch, a vote, a summit — need one day to produce a month of coverage.</span>

<span style="font-family: Arvo;"><strong>Unions</strong> want objects that come out again and again, because the same members turn up several times a year.</span>[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]<span style="font-family: Arvo;"><strong>NGOs and advocacy organisations</strong> need artwork that still works when volunteers in three cities are running it and there is no designer in the room. That means artwork files anyone can pick up.</span>

<span style="font-family: Arvo;"><strong>Political campaigns</strong> buy artwork and objects the way they buy everything else. <strong>Oddtoe</strong> has done fundraiser illustration for a US House candidate.</span>

<span style="font-family: Arvo;">Agencies working for any of the above are welcome too: see <strong><a class="dfd-custom-link-decorated" href="/experiential-marketing/">experiential marketing</a></strong>.</span>[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]<span style="font-family: Arvo;"><strong><a class="dfd-custom-link-decorated" href="/artist-designer/street-artist-muralist/">Street art</a></strong> is <strong>punk rock for visual artists</strong>. You do not need a gallery or a commission or anyone’s permission, and it gets seen by people who never decided to look at art that day.</span>

<span style="font-family: Arvo;">That is most of why this subject grabs me. A head carried down a street is doing the same job as a paste-up on a wall at four in the morning — putting the argument where people actually are.</span>[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]<span style="font-family: Arvo;">I make my own work as well as client work, and sculpture street art is where I want to take that next. So when a publicity stunt brief comes in, it is about the closest thing to what I would be making anyway.</span>

<span style="font-family: Arvo;">The practical upside for a campaign is that the person designing the object has <strong>a stake in whether it works</strong>. I want the photograph to be good for the same reason you do.</span>[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer artwork it came from, and the photos and video from the day. All of it is yours to keep, crate included, and it goes out again at the next action.</strong></span>

<span style="font-family: Arvo;">• <strong>The object</strong> — in this example four oversized heads, built light enough to carry
• <strong>The character artwork</strong> — the same designs flat, for placards, posters and social
• <strong>A crate</strong> it packs into and travels in
• <strong>Photos and video</strong> from the day, ready for news editors and for phones</span>[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]<span style="font-family: Arvo;">People tend to forget about the artwork. Because the object is built from finished character designs, the campaign also owns drawings that work on a poster, a placard, a t-shirt and a phone screen without redrawing anything.</span>

<span style="font-family: Arvo;">It can be whatever the idea needs: carried heads, a <strong><a class="dfd-custom-link-decorated" href="/artist-designer/inflatable-artist/">giant inflatable</a></strong>, a <strong><a class="dfd-custom-link-decorated" href="/artist-designer/mascot-designer/">mascot costume</a></strong>, a <strong><a class="dfd-custom-link-decorated" href="/artist-designer/kinetic-sculptor/">kinetic sculpture</a></strong>, or a <strong><a class="dfd-custom-link-decorated" href="/artist-designer/projection-artist/">projection</a></strong> on a building after dark, with the same characters <strong><a class="dfd-custom-link-decorated" href="/what-is-generative-ai-animation/">animated</a></strong>. They are designed together, so what goes up on the wall is the same character as the one in the street.</span>[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner You sign off on <strong>a picture of the thing</strong>, at the size it will be.</span></p>[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="24" screen_mobile_spacer_size="24"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/5"][vc_single_image image="16126" img_size="full" alignment="center" css=""][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="18" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="18" screen_tablet_spacer_size="14" screen_mobile_spacer_size="14"][dfd_heading content_alignment="text-center" enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" subtitle="Built, carried, landed?" subtitle_google_fonts="yes" subtitle_custom_fonts="font_family:Qwigley%3Aregular" title_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:26|font_family:BebasNeueRegular|line_height:28|letter_spacing:0" subtitle_font_options="tag:div|font_size:26|line_height:30|color:%23ddccb1" heading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;" subheading_margin="margin-bottom:2px;"]Feasibility[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text css=""]<p style="text-align: center;"><span style="font-family: Arvo;">Construction and weight. How volunteers move it. <strong>Customs, quarantine and freight</strong>, if it travels. And the date, which nobody can move.</span></p>[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="24" screen_mobile_spacer_size="24"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/5"][vc_single_image image="16125" img_size="full" alignment="center" css=""][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="18" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="18" screen_tablet_spacer_size="14" screen_mobile_spacer_size="14"][dfd_heading content_alignment="text-center" enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" subtitle="Built to travel" subtitle_google_fonts="yes" subtitle_custom_fonts="font_family:Qwigley%3Aregular" title_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:26|font_family:BebasNeueRegular|line_height:28|letter_spacing:0" subtitle_font_options="tag:div|font_size:26|line_height:30|color:%23ddccb1" heading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;" subheading_margin="margin-bottom:2px;"]Fabrication[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text css=""]<p style="text-align: center;"><span style="font-family: Arvo;">Designed in Melbourne, <strong>built by the right maker for the piece</strong>, here or near you. screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]<span style="font-family: Arvo;">A political cartoon and a publicity stunt photograph do the same job. You get about a second of someone’s attention, and if the picture needs explaining you have already lost them.</span>

<span style="font-family: Arvo;"><strong>Oddtoe</strong> drew editorial cartoons at college in Delaware, then worked as <strong>political cartoonist and chief designer</strong> for a Washington DC paper. Years of picking which single image a political story runs with, and watching an editor bin the ones that missed, usually for being too clever.</span>[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]<span style="font-family: Arvo;">More recently, an illustration and cover design for a US House candidate’s fundraiser — <strong>a donkey bullying an elephant</strong>. Blunt, and it still reads printed small.</span>

<span style="font-family: Arvo;">The same instinct decides what a stunt object should be. Out of <strong>twelve photographs</strong> from twelve actions, a news editor runs one. The job is to be that one.</span>

<span style="font-family: Arvo;">It also decides what to leave out. A head that needs a caption has failed, and so does one that turns into a blob from across a square.</span>[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" anchor="compare" dfd_row_responsive_enable="dfd-row-responsive-enable" responsive_styles="padding_left_mobile:10|padding_right_mobile:10"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="50" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_heading enable_delimiter="" style="style_02" title_font_options="tag:h2|font_size:90|font_family:BebasNeueRegular|line_height:84|letter_spacing:0" title_responsive="font_size_tablet:66|line_height_tablet:62|font_size_mobile:44|line_height_mobile:42" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_size:40|font_family:QwigleyRegular" subtitle="Where the money actually goes" heading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;"]Placards, a Stage, or Something Built?[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/6"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="2/3"][vc_column_text css=""]<span style="font-family: Arvo;">A campaign budget usually has one line for the visible part of an action. This is what that line buys three different ways.</span>
<div style="overflow-x: auto;">
<table style="width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse !important; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important;">
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="padding: 14px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 2px solid #ddccb1 !important; font-family: 'Bebas Neue', sans-serif; font-size: 21px; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: 1px; color: #ffffff !important; white-space: nowrap;" scope="col"></th>
<th style="padding: 14px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 2px solid #ddccb1 !important; font-family: 'Bebas Neue', sans-serif; font-size: 21px; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: 1px; color: #ffffff !important;" scope="col">Placards</th>
<th style="padding: 14px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 2px solid #ddccb1 !important; font-family: 'Bebas Neue', sans-serif; font-size: 21px; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: 1px; color: #ffffff !important;" scope="col">A hired stage</th>
<th style="padding: 14px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 2px solid #ddccb1 !important; font-family: 'Bebas Neue', sans-serif; font-size: 21px; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: 1px; color: #ffffff !important;" scope="col">Something built</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;"><strong>What it costs</strong></td>
<td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">Cheap per unit, spent again every action</td>
<td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">A large single-day hire</td>
<td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">One build, spread over years</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #140f0e !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;"><strong>How long it lasts</strong></td>
<td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #140f0e !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">One rally, if it does not rain</td>
<td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #140f0e !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">Gone by Monday morning</td>
<td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #140f0e !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">Years, in a crate between actions</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;"><strong>What a news editor does</strong></td>
<td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">Scrolls past it</td>
<td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">Crops it out of the frame</td>
<td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">Runs it, because nothing else looks like it</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #140f0e !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;"><strong>Who has to operate it</strong></td>
<td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #140f0e !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">Whoever is holding it</td>
<td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #140f0e !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">A crew and a technician</td>
<td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #140f0e !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">A few volunteers</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;"><strong>What you own afterwards</strong></td>
<td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">Nothing</td>
<td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">Nothing</td>
<td style="padding: 12px 18px; text-align: left; background-color: #000000 !important; border: none !important; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a2f2c !important; color: #ffffff !important;">The object and the character artwork</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/6"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay=""][vc_column width="1/4"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/2"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text item_animation="transition.fadeIn"]
<p style="text-align: center;"><span style="font-family: Qwigley; font-size: 36pt;">Questions about</span></p>
<p style="text-align: center;"><span style="font-family: 'Bebas Neue'; font-size: 36pt;">Publicity stunts?</span></p>
[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_accordion style="style-3" active_section="1" font_size="18" tab_title_google_fonts="yes" tab_title_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal" icon_size="14"][vc_tta_section title="What does this publicity stunt use case cover?" tab_id="1757300000001-usecase-protest-faq-1"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center;">A <strong>worked example</strong> of a publicity stunt. It follows one brief - a campaign with a press day and no picture - from the first question through design, fabrication, the day itself, and what the campaign still owns afterwards. It uses carried heads as the example, and an inflatable, a projection, a mascot costume or a kinetic sculpture would follow the same shape.</p>
[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="How long does a publicity stunt take?" tab_id="1757300000002-usecase-protest-faq-2"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center;"><strong>Six to eight weeks</strong> from brief to press day for a carried piece. Design and approval take the first fortnight, fabrication the next three weeks, and the rest is packing and freight. An inflatable or a mascot costume takes longer, because a specialist maker builds it from the drawings. A rush is possible but it comes out of the design stage, which is the part worth protecting.</p>
[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Can it be shipped outside Australia?" tab_id="1757300000003-usecase-protest-faq-3"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center;">Yes. Everything is built to crate, and freight and paperwork are part of the job. If a piece uses natural materials, the treatment and certification customs ask for get sorted from the start. Often the simpler answer is to build near you, working from the drawings.</p>
[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="What does a publicity stunt cost?" tab_id="1757300000004-usecase-protest-faq-4"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center;"><strong>Oddtoe</strong> does not publish prices. Cost is driven by what the object is, how many, how large, how much structure each one needs, and where it has to travel. It is costed the same way as any other <strong><a class="dfd-custom-link-decorated" href="/prop-fabrication-services/">prop fabrication</a></strong> job. Send the brief and the date and you get a quote.</p>
[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Do we need council permits?" tab_id="1757300000005-usecase-protest-faq-5"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center;">Usually not for the objects themselves - they are carried, not installed, with no power and no rigging. The permit conversation is about the assembly or the march, which the campaign is already having.</p>
[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Can we use it more than once?" tab_id="1757300000006-usecase-protest-faq-6"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center;">That is the point. It goes back in the crate and comes out at the next action. An object built for one press day has usually paid for itself by its <strong>third outing</strong>.</p>
[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Can you do the animation and projection as well?" tab_id="1757300000007-usecase-protest-faq-7"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center;">Yes, and they are designed together when the brief calls for it - the same characters animated and projected after dark. See <strong><a class="dfd-custom-link-decorated" href="/artist-designer/projection-artist/">projection art</a></strong> and <strong><a class="dfd-custom-link-decorated" href="/what-is-generative-ai-animation/">generative AI animation</a></strong>.</p>
[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Where is Oddtoe based?" tab_id="1757300000008-usecase-protest-faq-8"][vc_column_text css=""]
<p style="text-align: center;"><strong>Oddtoe</strong> is based in Melbourne, Australia. Supplier and business contacts run through Berlin and Los Angeles, and those are the starting points for work in Europe and the United States.</p>
[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][/dfd_accordion][vc_raw_html][/vc_raw_html][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_button button_text="Contact Oddtoe" buttom_link_src="url:https%3A%2F%2Fwww.oddtoe.com%2Fcontact-oddtoe%2F|title:Contact%20Oddtoe" background="#8a8f6a" hover_background="#4e5041" border="border-style:none;|border-radius:5px;" hover_border="border-style:none;|border-radius:5px;" style="style_6"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="110" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="90" screen_tablet_spacer_size="60" screen_mobile_spacer_size="60"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/4"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay="" one_page_title="More" anchor="more"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="100" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="90" screen_tablet_spacer_size="80" screen_mobile_spacer_size="80"][vc_column_text css="" item_animation="transition.fadeIn"]
<p style="text-align: center;"><span style="font-family: Qwigley; font-size: 36pt;">Interested in seeing more… </span></p>
